where: crates/blaze-engine/src/engine.rs over overlay.rs; last.rs (the seam); blaze-cli engine_answer_rows.rs (RowsAnswer, PagesAnswer)
what: Making the engine generic over the last answer (Engine<'a, S, L = Answer>) needed more from the seam than its first cut gave: the whole digest a row saw of each read (the engine names `Cause::ReadMoved { was, now }` and compares digests, so a cell that moved and moved back leaves its readers standing), the digest a task reads through its view (32 bytes; the rows form keeps 20), when a cell last moved, and whether an owed task's row was ever made (the seam returned an owed-no-row as a row with flag OWED, which the engine would read as `Cause::KeyMoved` instead of `Cause::New`). Added `seen`, `content`, `moved` and `Flags::UNMADE`. PagesAnswer::saw also binary-searched a read list that is in read order, not cell order.
cost: most of the lane's design time went into the seam's gaps before the overlay could be a pure substitution; nothing compiled in-lane (write-only)
cause: the seam was written from the rows form's columns, not from what engine.rs asks
whys: no form behind the seam was the engine's own in-memory answer, so no test held a seam answer against the engine's own lookups
class: an interface cut from the implementation's storage, not from its caller's questions
prevention: done: `impl LastAnswer for Answer` (last_mem.rs) is the default form, and last_sim.rs runs every history on Engine<Answer> and Engine<SimLast> and holds them equal; a planted bug in the overlay (Plant::ReadersStale) is the control. Not done: the rows form (generation rule, 20-byte digests) is held to the engine by no oracle yet
annoyance: write-only lane without Grep/Glob tools: read-only grep/sed through Bash only
workaround: grep/sed -n through Bash, as the lane rules allow
